import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for each feature
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        mean1 = np.mean(x[y == 1])
        mean0 = np.mean(x[y == 0])
        effect = mean1 - mean0
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y == 1], x[y == 0], equal_var=False)
        effects.append((fid, effect, abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size (descending)
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = []
    used = set()
    for fid, effect, tstat, pval in effects:
        if fid in used:
            continue
        keep.append((fid, effect, tstat, pval))
        # Mark correlated features as used
        for other_fid, _, _, _ in effects:
            if other_fid != fid and other_fid not in used:
                try:
                    corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], 
                                       feats.x[:, feats.column(other_fid)])[0,1]
                    if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                        used.add(other_fid)
                except:
                    pass
        used.add(fid)
    
    # Select top features for regression (max 10)
    top_features = [f[0] for f in keep[:min(10, len(keep))]]
    
    # If no features selected, return empty design
    if not top_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Fit logistic regression to identify drivers
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in top_features]]
    model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', random_state=0)
    model.fit(X, feats.y)
    
    # Get coefficients and select drivers
    coefs = model.coef_[0]
    driver_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(coefs))[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    drivers = []
    for i in driver_indices:
        if i < len(top_features) and abs(coefs[i]) > 0.01:
            drivers.append(top_features[i])
    
    # Build columns, products, and loadings
    columns = top_features
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(top_features):
        if i < len(coefs) and abs(coefs[i]) > 0.01:
            loadings[fid] = coefs[i]
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
